summary.text: In Mandarin, 了 commonly marks completed action or a change of state. Its pictorial origin is disputed: the received account describes 子 without arms, while a later commentary interprets the form as crossed or entangled legs. The connection between these interpretations and “finish” remains unresolved.

formation.text: The received historical account treats 了 as a pictograph related to 子, described as 子 without arms. A later commentary instead interprets the image as crossed or entangled legs. These competing readings do not securely identify the original referent.

history.text: The received explanation describes 了 as 子 without arms; a later commentary interprets its image through crossed or entangled legs. The available accounts do not establish a securely dated earliest graph or a sequence of graphic changes.

uncertainties.text: The relation between the pictorial interpretations and the historical sense “finish” is unresolved. A sound-based reuse of the graph has been proposed, as has a semantic path from entanglement to completion, but neither is demonstrated here.

The reported Tang–Song grammatical development is summarized in secondary and scholarly accounts; exact dated examples are not supplied. A possible later interaction between sentence-final 了 and 也 in some dialects remains tentative.

senses.text: The received entry glosses 了 with 尦; a later commentary interprets this as legs crossing or becoming entangled. This is a historical interpretation of the graph, not direct confirmation of what an early inscription depicted.

Historical dictionary citations include “finish; be completed,” with the Tang phrase 未了 meaning “not ended” or “not finished.” The earliest attestation and the link to the pictorial interpretations remain unresolved.

senses.period: common by Tang; later stages summarized for Tang–Song
senses.text: The completed-action marker is described as developing from the verb “finish,” with resultative uses in between and aspect-marking examples in Song accounts.

senses.period: dating unresolved; later than perfective use in the reported account
senses.text: A further development from the perfective particle produced the sentence-final change-of-state use. Its detailed path remains uncertain, including a proposed interaction with 也 in some dialects.

developments.text: The completed-action marker is described as a grammatical development of the verb “finish,” with resultative uses along the way.
The sentence-final change-of-state use is described as developing from the perfective use; a possible interaction with 也 is proposed for some dialects, but the details remain unresolved.

limitations.text: The evidence does not resolve whether “finish” became associated with the graph through sound-based reuse or a semantic path from the proposed entangled-legs interpretation. No early spelling or dated intermediate examples settle the question.
Later dictionary citations report both “understand clearly” and “finish,” but do not establish their relative chronology or a semantic connection.

overview.text: In Mandarin, 了 commonly marks completed action or change of state. A proposed sound-based reuse is that the old word for the depicted form may have sounded like “finish,” but that word and sound match are unverified.

takeaway.text: The proposed borrowing offers a possible explanation for “finish”; a semantic route through “entangled” has also been suggested, but neither account is established.
